newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling slips vs dlr but still seen bullish.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling slips vs dlr but still seen bullish.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened against the dollar on Tuesday in dull trading, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) posted a shiling mean rate of 56.61 against the dollar from 56.50 on Monday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 88.18 from 88.21 on Monday.
"Position squaring and an upsurge in demand drove the local unit lower versus the dollar in late afternoon trade," a dealer said. "From 56.40/60, the shilling tended weaker to 56.48/68."

"However, volumes were thin and trade dull in the day. Sentiment for the shilling remains bullish as exporter sales continue to outstrip demand from importers," she added. "The range for the day is 56.40/70."
Bankers said they expected importers to return back into the market so that the shilling could recoup it's earlier loses.
Dealers said overnight money market was tight with rates qouted above 20 percent.
